Objectives To investigate whether repeated ketamine exposure during adolescence may influence the long-term risk of addiction following subsequent exposure to commonly abused drugs (alcohol and cocaine) in adulthood. Methods Male and female Sprague-Dawley rats received daily i.p. injections of ketamine (10 mg/kg) or saline for 7 consecutive days during mid adolescence. The dose paradigm of ketamine administered was selected based on its antidepressant-like properties in adolescent rats. In adulthood, addiction liability was measured by voluntary ethanol consumption, using a two-bottle choice paradigm, and by assessing cocaine reward using a single-exposure place preference protocol. Results The main results suggested that a therapeutic dose of ketamine exposure during adolescence did not enhance addictive liability in adulthood as measured by voluntary ethanol consumption or cocaine reward in rats of both sexes. Conclusions Ketamine, administered during adolescence at a dose known to induce antidepressant-like effects did not impact the long-term risk of addiction caused by exposure to commonly abused drugs (i.e., alcohol and cocaine). These results suggested a good long-term safety profile following the therapeutic use of ketamine in adolescence.

articles.title: The decoction of licorice, ginseng, and dry ginger demonstrates anti-pulmonary fibrosis activity through modulation of the pyroptosis pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a chronic progressive lung disease that causes damage to the lung structure and respiratory failure. Currently, there is no effective cure for this condition. The "Licorice dried ginger ginseng soup" (LGGS) recorded in Volume 3 of "Xianzheng Bingzhi" is a traditional prescription used to treat lung atrophy. However, the pharmacological mechanism of its effect on pulmonary fibrosis has not been studied yet. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to explore the protective effects of LGGS when administered separately as silica and bleomycin in the mouse lung fibrosis model, to reveal its mechanism of action, and to focus on the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD signaling pathway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis were induced in C57BL/6 mice using silica and bleomycin, respectively, and LGGS was administered as intervention. Lung function, histopathology, and serum metabolites were evaluated. The major component contents in LGGS were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Western blotting was performed to verify the molecular mechanism. RESULTS: LGGS significantly reduced the degree of pulmonary fibrosis in both silica- and bleomycin-induced mouse models, improved lung function, and decreased hydroxyproline (HYP) content in lung tissues. The established HPLC method effectively determined the main components with good linearity. LGGS down-regulated the protein expression of α-SMA, COL1, Caspase-1, GSDMD, and NLRP3. CONCLUSION: LGGS exerts anti-pulmonary fibrosis effects, potentially by inhibiting the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptosis pathway. The HPLC method is accurate and reliable, providing a basis for quality control of LGGS.

articles.title: Linarin ameliorates bisphenol A-induced prostatic primary ciliogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition via reducing stromal exosome circ_0027470.
articles.abstract: Changes in epithelial features are the crucial pathological phenomena in many prostatic diseases. Previous studies elucidated the negative effects of bisphenol A (BPA) on regulating exosome-mediated epithelium-mesenchyme communication. This study investigated the effects of linarin, a natural flavonoid, on BPA-induced epithelium changes in mouse prostate, as well as in a co-culture system of human epithelial-stromal cells. The visualized evaluation for mouse prostatic collagen deposition was performed via Masson and Sirius red staining. The characteristics of prostate epithelium including primary ciliogenesis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and circ_0027470/miR-1236-3p/Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) axis were evaluated through immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, qPCR and western blotting. The results showed that linarin attenuated epithelial primary ciliogenesis and EMT which were triggered by BPA-exposed stromal exosomes. Additionally, linarin reduced the circ_0027470 level, increased the miR-1236-3p level, and inhibited the activity of the Sonic Hedgehog signaling pathway. This study added new evidence for the application of linarin in improving prostatic injuries caused by BPA.

articles.title: Development of an adverse outcome pathway (AOP): Stimulation of toll-like receptor (TLR) 7/8 induces psoriatic skin disease.
articles.abstract: The Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) framework serves as a vital tool in regulatory toxicology, providing a structured approach for understanding the mechanistic links between chemical exposure and adverse health outcomes. This AOP specifically addresses the pathway leading to psoriatic skin disease, initiated by the stimulation of Toll-like receptors 7 and 8 (TLR7/8), which triggers a cascade of key events (KEs). The sequence begins with the maturation of TNF/iNOS-producing dendritic cells, leading to increased interleukin-23 (IL-23) production, which subsequently drives Th17 cell migration and inflammation. Ultimately, these processes culminate in the manifestation of psoriatic skin disease as the adverse outcome (AO). This AOP was developed according to OECD guidance for AOP development through the integration and evaluation of published mechanistic evidence. Relevant information was assembled using an iterative literature review approach, and the biological plausibility, essentiality, and empirical support for each key event relationship (KER) were evaluated using a weight-of-evidence framework based on modified Bradford-Hill considerations. The resulting AOP highlights mechanistically supported relationships among TLR7/8 stimulation, dendritic cell activation, IL-23 production, and Th17-mediated inflammation, supported by evidence evaluated according to OECD AOP principles. By integrating existing data and mechanistic insights, this AOP not only enhances our understanding of the pathophysiology of psoriatic skin disease but also aids in the regulatory assessment of chemicals that may trigger these pathways. This AOP broadens the AOP network, particularly with respect to autoimmune skin disease. Additionally, this AOP represents a significant step toward expanding AOPs related to immunotoxicity.

articles.title: Coptisine attenuates gastric mucosal injury by activating the PPARα signaling pathway to inhibit ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury is a common and highly recurrent gastrointestinal disorder. Coptisine exerts a confirmed protective effect on the gastric mucosa, yet its underlying mechanism of action remains elusive to date. OBJECTIVE: The present research aims to explore how coptisine confers protection on the gastric mucosa from ethanol-mediated damage and to unravel the intrinsic mechanisms responsible for this effect. METHODS: Network pharmacology screened key targets and pathways, and molecular docking plus dynamics simulations analyzed compound-protein binding properties. A mouse model of ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury was established, and coptisine was administered intragastrically for one week continuously. The protective effect on gastric mucosa and the impact on ferroptosis and the PPARα signaling pathway were evaluated through HE staining, biochemical indicators, immunohistochemistry, Western blotting (WB), and transmission electron microscopy. GES-1 cells were cultured, and cell viability, apoptosis, and mitochondrial membrane potential were evaluated. RESULTS: Coptisine significantly protects against ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury. It suppresses inflammation and oxidative stress and inhibits apoptosis by modulating related protein expression. Coptisine modulates ferroptosis-related molecules and PPARα signaling, improves GES-1 cell viability, attenuates ROS accumulation, recovers mitochondrial function, and relieves cell apoptosis. These findings demonstrate that coptisine exerts gastric mucosal protection by activating the PPARα pathway and inhibiting ferroptosis. CONCLUSION: Our research reports, for the first time, that coptisine possesses the capacity to prevent and ameliorate ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury. Regulation of apoptosis and ferroptosis in gastric epithelial cells via the PPARα signaling pathway constitutes the key mechanism underlying this process.

articles.title: Oxaliplatin-induced redox imbalance and lipid remodeling are associated with altered steroid-related responses in spermatogenic cells.
articles.abstract: Oxaliplatin (OXA) is a cornerstone of colorectal cancer therapy, but its effects on male germ cell metabolism and signaling remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the effects of OXA on redox homeostasis, lipid-related processes, and steroid-related responses in GC-1 (spg) and GC-2 (spd) spermatogenic cells. OXA exposure induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial depolarization together with pronounced changes in lipid organization and signaling pathways. Notably, instead of inducing overt lipid peroxidation, OXA prompted neutral lipid accumulation and increased intracellular free cholesterol, accompanied by changes in proteins involved in lipid and cholesterol homeostasis. These alterations were accompanied by modulation of lipid-metabolic regulators, including increased expression of ACOX1, consistent with alterations in peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism. The metabolic perturbations were further associated with stage-specific activation of signaling cascades and altered intracellular testosterone levels. Importantly, antioxidant intervention attenuated oxidative stress but did not fully reverse the observed lipid-related and steroid-related responses, suggesting that redox regulation may contribute to these changes but does not fully explain the cellular response to OXA. Collectively, our findings indicate that OXA exposure is associated with coordinated changes in redox balance, lipid-related processes, and steroid-related responses in spermatogenic cells, revealing cell type-specific differences in their response to chemotherapy.

articles.title: LGA-PEI nanoparticles enable efficient nucleic acid delivery to primary murine T cells.
articles.abstract: Non-viral engineering of primary T cells is constrained by low transfection efficiency and significant cargo-induced toxicity. This study evaluates a LGA-PEI (lactic-co-glycolic acid-modified polyethyleneimine) nanoparticle system designed to overcome the recalcitrance of murine T cells, particularly unstimulated, murine T cells. We characterized LGA-PEI polyplexes for size, surface charge, and pH-dependent stability, noting rapid disassembly at pH 5.0 to facilitate endosomal escape. Optimization of nanoparticle concentrations enabled transfection efficiencies of 16.5 % in CD3-sensitized T cells and 30.0 % in stimulated primary mouse T cells, maintaining high viability (85 %). Mechanistic analysis suggests that cell death is primarily driven by initial membrane disruption rather than post-internalization metabolic stress. We identified a direct correlation between the number of internalized plasmids and GFP expression, confirming efficient post-internalization events. LGA-PEI-mediated delivery of shRNA targeting Sorcin achieved significant gene knockdown. Transfection with LGA-PEI-encapsulated scrambled control plasmids (shRNA) exhibited increased CD25 and FoxP3 marker expression, along with cytokine production alterations. These findings demonstrate that the LGA-PEI platform provides a high-efficiency, low-toxicity alternative for T cell modulation, though the observed phenotypic alterations necessitate careful immunotoxicity screening in therapeutic applications.

articles.title: Transferrin functionalization enhances prostate cancer cell uptake and cytotoxicity of cabazitaxel-loaded polymeric nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second most common cancer in men worldwide, and chemotherapeutic treatment may exhibit limited efficacy owing to side effects and hypersensitivity. Cabazitaxel (CTX) is an antineoplastic agent used to treat prostate cancer; however, it has low selectivity and adverse effects that limit its adherence and efficacy. In this context, transferrin (Tf)-functionalized polymeric nanoparticles have emerged as a potential targeted therapy directed toward the Tf receptor (TfR), which is overexpressed in prostate cancer cells. In this study, cabazitaxel was encapsulated in polycaprolactone (PCL) polymeric nanoparticles functionalized with transferrin (Tf), and its in vitro activity was evaluated in PCa cell lines. Therefore, a study was conducted to determine the optimal preparation conditions in terms of formulation characteristics. The nanoparticles were produced by nanoprecipitation using acetone as the solvent in the presence of the surfactant Poloxamer 188. Transferrin was covalently bound to the PEG-PCL-maleimide moiety on the nanoparticle surface. The transferrin-functionalized nanoparticles had an average particle size of 123.9 nm ± 1.13, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.168 ± 0.11, a zeta potential of -11.43 mV ± 1.89, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE%) of 79.6% ± 6.8. In electrophoresis, free transferrin exhibited a band near 80 kDa, with a corresponding band observed in the elution of the functionalized nanoparticles, indicating protein attachment to the nanoparticles. Circular dichroism analysis, together with fluorescence spectroscopy, demonstrated the preservation of protein structural integrity after conjugation. Microscopy techniques (SEM and AFM) revealed the spherical morphology of the nanoparticles, and AFM further confirmed successful conjugation through changes in the surface roughness of the functionalized nanoparticles. The in vitro release study demonstrated that both non-functionalized and transferrin-functionalized PCL-based nanoparticles provided a sustained release of cabazitaxel over 192 h, confirming the potential of these systems for prolonged drug delivery. In cell culture assays, the high cell viability observed in the L929 cell line demonstrated the safety of the developed systems, whereas the marked reduction in viability in DU145 and PC3 cell lines demonstrated the effect of encapsulation on cytotoxicity of the developed systems. Functionalization with transferrin (Tf) significantly increased the in vitro toxicity and cellular internalization. The percentage of cellular internalization was higher in the PC3 cell line than in the DU145 cell line, corroborating the literature reporting higher TfR expression in this lineage. Encapsulation and functionalization demonstrated potential as active drug-targeting vectors, as they increased cytotoxicity compared to free drugs. This finding represents an important advancement in the development of a formulation and approach capable of enhancing therapeutic efficacy while reducing the systemic side effects of the drug.

articles.title: Impact of the protein corona in RGD-functionalized nanoliposomes delivering enzymatic replacement therapy for Fabry disease.
articles.abstract: The protein corona (PC) formed upon nanoparticle exposure to blood critically defines their biological identity and in vivo fate, yet its impact on targeted liposomal enzyme replacement therapies (ERTs) remains incompletely understood. Here, we systematically investigated how RGD functionalization (including varying ligand densities) and α-galactosidase A (GLA) loading influence PC composition, cellular uptake, and biodistribution using a panel of liposomal formulations with and without targeting ligands and therapeutic cargo. Quantitative proteomics revealed that both RGD functionalization and GLA loading reshape the PC by enriching key opsonins (e.g., C3 and IgG subclasses) together with dysopsonins (such as apolipoproteins and albumin), generating distinct and balanced immune signatures. Notably, RGD promoted complement recruitment, indicating increased immune recognition potential. In vitro, RGD functionalization significantly enhanced endothelial uptake even in the presence of a pre-formed PC, demonstrating that targeting functionality is modulated but not abolished by corona formation. In vivo, GLA-loaded liposomes increased enzymatic activity in plasma and tissues compared to free GLA, and higher RGD density enhanced delivery to liver, spleen, kidney, and heart, albeit with reduced plasma persistence. All GLA-loaded formulations showed brain-associated enzymatic activity in perfused brain tissue. Additional capillary-depletion analysis indicated that, at 30 min after administration, the measurable signal was predominantly associated with the cerebrovascular fraction, that could be potentially linked to coronas enriched in ApoE, transferrin, and transthyretin. Together, these findings support a hybrid model in which the protein corona modulates, rather than masks, targeting ligands through a balanced opsonin/dysopsonin profile. This work provides mechanistic insight into how nanoparticle surface properties and biological identity interplay, offering general design principles for optimizing targeted nanomedicines beyond liposomal ERT.

articles.title: Calixarene-based nanocarrier for ciprofloxacin and curcumin: evaluation of antibacterial, antibiofilm, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.
articles.abstract: Drug delivery and multidrug therapy are essential research fields in the fight against complex diseases, including infections. Here, we investigated the capability of a polyanionic nanocarrier, formed through the spontaneous self-assembly of an amphiphilic p-sulfonate-calix[4]arene derivative, to load ciprofloxacin and curcumin, both individually and in combination, using a simple and reproducible organic solvent-free method. Entrapment in the nanocarrier enhanced the aqueous solubility and stability of both ciprofloxacin and curcumin and protected them from UV light-induced photodegradation. The supramolecular nanosized assemblies exhibited antibacterial activity against Gram-positive (S. aureus ATCC 6538) and Gram-negative (Escherichia coli ATCC 10536, P. aeruginosa ATCC 9027) bacteria, including antibiotic-resistant strains (S. aureus (MRSA) ATCC 43300, S. aureus 1199B, Enterococcus faecium DSM 17050, Acinetobacter baumannii DSM 106838, E. coli DSM 105388, and P. aeruginosa DSM 102273). Against S. aureus 1199B, the nanoassemblies reduced biofilm formation, an effect largely attributable to the empty nanocarrier, and were effective against mature biofilms. The antioxidant activity of curcumin was preserved following its incorporation into the nanocarrier, as demonstrated by its DPPH radical scavenging activity. Additionally, the nanoassemblies loaded with ciprofloxacin and curcumin showed anti-inflammatory effects, as evidenced by the reduced TNF-α levels in LPS-stimulated eukaryotic cells. The multifunctional nature of the nanoassemblies highlights their potential for combining antimicrobial, radical-scavenging and anti-inflammatory properties, offering a promising approach to addressing the complex challenges associated with bacterial infections, including those involving biofilms.

articles.title: Dynamic stratum corneum ceramide alterations reflect barrier dysfunction and clinical response to topical chlormethine treatment in early-stage mycosis fungoides.
articles.abstract: Early-stage mycosis fungoides (MF), a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, presents as patches and/or plaques with an impaired skin barrier. The stratum corneum (SC) lipid matrix is important for skin barrier function. Alterations in the SC ceramide profile have been linked to a reduced barrier function in benign inflammatory skin diseases and might also be an underlying factor in the impaired barrier function in MF. Therefore, we characterized barrier function and SC ceramide profiles in lesional and non-lesional skin of 21 patients with early-stage MF and 10 healthy controls, and assessed how these barrier and ceramide characteristics evolve during chlormethine gel treatment in patients. Barrier function was measured by transepidermal water loss. SC ceramides were collected by tape stripping and analyzed by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Local inflammatory markers were measured in suction blister fluid. At baseline, MF lesions showed impaired barrier function accompanied by distinct changes in the SC ceramide profile, including altered ceramide subclass composition and reduced ceramide chain length. These abnormalities occurred in the context of a predominantly type 1-skewed inflammatory milieu. Importantly, both barrier dysfunction and ceramide alterations were dynamic and improved in patients with a clinical response to chlormethine gel treatment, alongside reduced lesion severity and local inflammation. Longitudinal associations of ceramide characteristics with barrier function, clinical lesion severity, and inflammatory markers support SC ceramide alterations as dynamic correlates of MF disease activity. Together, these findings suggest that SC ceramide alterations may reflect a downstream consequence of inflammation that is shared across inflammatory dermatoses.

articles.title: Comparison of bupivacaine concentrations in local tissue from three extended-release formulations in a pig incision model.
articles.abstract: This study measured bupivacaine distribution in subcutaneous (SC) tissue and skin after administration of the commercially available extended-release local anesthetics ERLAs liposomal bupivacaine (Lip-Bupi) and polyorthoester bupivacaine-meloxicam (POE-Bupi-Mel), an investigational temperature-responsive gel formulation (SBG004) by subcutaneous (SC) injection or wound filling (WF), and 0.25% bupivacaine HCl. Each ERLA was administered to six skin and muscle incisions in pigs surviving for 24, 48, or 72 h. Samples of skin or SC tissue representing 2 mm intervals from the incision were analyzed for bupivacaine concentration. Average bupivacaine concentration in each tissue within 10 mm of the incision ([BUPI]SC,10mm or [BUPI]skin,10mm) was compared between formulations. SBG004 SC resulted in higher [BUPI]SC,10mm versus each other formulation at each time point (P < 0.01). Average [BUPI]SC,10mm for SBG004 SC was 15 to 52-fold greater than Lip-Bupi and at least 64-fold greater than POE-Bupi-Mel (at 72 h: SBG004 SC 1,250 ± 580 µg/g; Lip-Bupi 24 ± 28 µg/g; POE-Bupi-Mel 20 ± 21 µg/g). Concentration differences in skin were similar but of a lower magnitude. The results indicate that injection in surgical wound margins and remaining in situ throughout the duration of release contribute to sustaining higher local anesthetic concentrations in tissue.

articles.title: Development of pH-Responsive Curcumin-Loaded nanofiber composites with AI-Assisted color recognition for wound dressing.
articles.abstract: A novel pH-responsive curcumin-loaded nanofiber composite with artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted color recognition for therapeutic delivery and intelligent visual monitoring was developed for application in smart wound dressings. Smart wound dressings were developed by integrating curcumin electrospray microparticles (Cur/MPs) and polycaprolactone/chitosan (PCL/CS) nanofibers using a dual-process strategy involving electrospray and electrospinning by the Taguchi method. Zein was the biocompatible carrier to enhance curcumin stability and regulate its sustained release. The curcumin electrospray microparticles@polycaprolactone/chitosan (Cur/MPs@PCL/CS) nanofiber composites exhibited tunable hydrophilicity, over 90% porosity, good cell viability with 125.1 ± 2.0%, and visible inhibition of Escherichia coli growth under the tested plate-diffusion conditions, indicating the suitability of these composites for biomedical dressings. Curcumin release followed first-order kinetics with dual-stage release, prolonging bioactivity. The visible pH-dependent color change of curcumin suggests potential for pH-responsive wound monitoring, and AI-assisted image classification may reduce subjective interpretation under controlled imaging conditions. The VISDEEP-C2 model (batch = 5, epochs = 100, learning rate = 10-4), optimized via Taguchi design, achieved an initial accuracy of 91.03% and rose to 99.28% after the dataset was expanded to 1,360 images. The synergistic integration of intelligent sensing, controlled drug release, and antimicrobial functionality positions Cur/MPs@PCL/CS as a promising next-generation smart wound-care material. This intelligent, biocompatible nanocomposite platform contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3: Good Health and Well-Being and SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) by promoting sustainable biomedical materials and AI-driven healthcare innovation.

articles.title: Estrogen receptor modulation by a newly-identified cannabinoid in a preclinical model of breast cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast cancer is a diverse group of diseases comprising subtypes with distinct behavior and response to therapy. Tumors that express estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) and depend on estrogen constitute ∼65% of all breast cancer cases. Common endocrine therapy for this kind of breast cancer includes Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators (SERMs) such as tamoxifen. However, despite the clear benefits, many patients do not complete the recommended 5 and sometimes 10 years of treatment because of adverse effects. Medical cannabis is increasingly used by cancer patients, primarily for palliative care, yet its direct antitumor potential in breast cancer remains poorly understood. PURPOSE: Examine whether cannabis-derived compounds exert selective antitumor effects in breast cancer and elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. STUDY DESIGN: A combination of in vitro experiments in multiple ER-positive breast cancer cell lines with in vivo validation in an estrogen-dependent xenograft mouse model. METHODS: Breast cancer cell lines representing different molecular subtypes were evaluated. A panel of chemically distinct cannabis extracts was initially screened for cytotoxic activity and subsequently tested in combination with SERMs. Extracts were chemically profiled using ESI-LC/MS. Phytocannabinoid fractionation, chemical analyses, and structural elucidation were performed to isolate and characterize the bioactive phytocannabinoid in the only cannabis extract identified in the initial screen as effective in combination with tamoxifen. The mechanism of action of this phytocannabinoid was investigated in vitro using molecular and biochemical assays. Finally, antitumor efficacy was assessed in vivo using an estrogen-dependent ER-positive breast cancer xenograft mouse model. RESULTS: We found a unique cannabis extract, CANN14, capable of sensitizing ER-positive breast cancer cells to the cytotoxic effect of tamoxifen. We identified a novel phytocannabinoid 373.15b that mimicked the effect of the whole extract without any toxicity by itself. It has a unique structure of a dihydroxyphenol with an acetate group attached to the aromatic ring, distinguishing it from known cannabinoid scaffolds. Cannabinoid 373.15b modulated estrogen signaling by decreasing the mRNA and protein expression levels of ERα, as well as its transcriptional activity, possibly through a signaling pathway involving RASSF1A and Hippo signaling components. In an in vivo mouse model, treatment with 373.15b reduced tumor volume and weight, with a more profound effect when combined with tamoxifen. CONCLUSION: The work presented here identifies a novel cannabinoid that modulates ERα signaling and enhances the antitumor efficacy of SERMs. The findings suggests that co-therapy of 373.15b with SERMs may allow dose reduction of conventional therapy, and by that, diminish the associated adverse effects and improve patient quality of life. ONE-SENTENCE SUMMARY: The newly identified cannabinoid 373.15b reduces ERα expression and activity through RASSF1A and Hippo signaling pathway thus exerting antitumor effects.

articles.title: Interleukin-17D Deficiency Attenuates Atherosclerosis by Diminishing Macrophage Inflammation and Promoting M2 Phenotype.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Macrophages are central to atherosclerosis by driving vascular inflammation, plaque growth, and instability. Although interleukin-17D (IL-17D) has been linked to endothelial inflammation, its role in macrophage-mediated atherosclerosis remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated the function and mechanism of macrophage IL-17D in atherosclerosis. METHODS: Using IL-17D knockout, macrophage-specific IL-17D knockdown, and macrophage-specific Spi-B knockdown mouse models on an ApoE-/- background, we assessed aortic lesion burden, necrotic core formation, macrophage accumulation, inflammatory responses, and macrophage polarization. Mechanistic studies were performed using transcriptomic analysis, ChIP-PCR, and luciferase reporter assays. RESULTS: IL-17D deficiency markedly reduced atherosclerotic plaque formation in the whole aorta and aortic root, decreased necrotic core size, and limited macrophage accumulation and vascular inflammation. Both in vitro and in vivo, IL-17D deficiency promoted M2 macrophage polarization while suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Macrophage-specific IL-17D knockdown similarly attenuated atherosclerotic lesion development and inflammation. Mechanistically, IL-17D deficiency activated the Spi-B-STAT6 transcriptional axis. Macrophage-specific Spi-B knockdown reversed the anti-atherosclerotic effects of IL-17D deficiency, confirming its functional importance. Rosuvastatin suppressed IL-17D expression, and IL-17D repression contributed to its anti-inflammatory and anti-atherogenic effects. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify macrophage-derived IL-17D as a key regulator of atherosclerosis. Targeting IL-17D may promote protective M2 polarization and alleviate vascular inflammation, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for atherosclerotic disease.

articles.title: A machine learning-based model for predicting the color of liquid formulation placebos and analyzing their visual similarity.
articles.abstract: High-quality randomized, placebo-controlled trials are critical for clinical drug trials, but preparing color‑matched placebos for liquid formulations remains difficult due to the color complexity of liquid formulations and the inefficiency of conventional matching methods. Machine learning offers an effective approach to modeling the complex non-linear relationships among multiple colorants at varying concentrations, enabling prediction of color formulations. This study employed optimal Latin hypercube sampling to generate 253 simulated samples with five colorants. After color correction using a correction matrix, ten color space values were extracted for model fitting. Among five models, random forest (RF) performed best, with a mean absolute error of 0.09, a root mean square error of 0.15, and an R2 value of 0.69. Shapley additive explanations analysis identified L*, G, gray, and V as key variables influencing the prediction of placebo color formulations. Validation against eight target solutions produced average color differences of ΔEab = 3.35 and ΔE00 = 2.20, and a mean visual similarity score of 9.1 by human assessors, indicating a relatively high prediction accuracy. This study developed an RF‑based strategy for predicting the color of placebo in liquid formulations, enabling visual color matching with test drugs in clinical trials.

articles.title: Bovine serum Albumin-Mediated effects on colonic Solubility, mucus Permeation, and absorption of celecoxib.
articles.abstract: Celecoxib was used as a model compound in fasted state simulated colonic fluid (FaSSCoF) to investigate equilibrium drug solubility (Seq), protein binding using rapid equilibrium dialysis (RED), flux and permeability (Papp) across porcine colonic mucus (PCM), and in vivo colonic absorption using a rat intracolonic instillation model. The primary focus was on the role of bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a solubilizing and binding constituent, while bile salts (sodium taurodeoxycholate, TDC) with lecithin and poloxamer 407 were included as comparative systems to evaluate how differences in solubilizer type influence celecoxib permeability and absorption. BSA demonstrated a pronounced solubilizing effect on celecoxib with a 1:1 M binding ratio, increasing the apparent Seq from 5.1 µg/mL to 92 µg/mL in FaSSCoF containing 15 mg/mL BSA. Under these conditions, diffusion across PCM increased approximately seven-fold compared with FaSSCoF without BSA, accompanied by a four-fold increase in colonic absorption in vivo. In contrast, when celecoxib concentration was maintained constant and BSA was subsequently added to FaSSCoF, diffusion across PCM decreased up to ten-fold at BSA concentrations of 1.5 mg/mL, accompanied by an approximately 30 % decrease in colonic absorption in vivo. This behavior is consistent with an increased BSA-bound fraction and a reduced free drug concentration available for transport. The addition of TDC with lecithin or poloxamer 407 similarly increased celecoxib diffusion across PCM and colonic absorption when celecoxib was dissolved at Seq in FaSSCoF, although no statistically significant differences were observed between the solubilizing systems. Overall, these findings demonstrate that solubilizing constituents in colonic fluids can substantially increase drug solubility, mucus permeation, and colonic absorption, highlighting the importance of accounting for protein-drug interactions when evaluating drug behavior in the colon.

articles.title: Minthostachys verticillata aqueous extract ameliorates intestinal and systemic alterations induced by a model of acute stress.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGIC RELEVANCE: Minthostachys verticillata (Griseb.) Epling (Lamiaceae), popularly known as Peperina (Mv), is a native plant widely used in traditional medicine as a digestive, sedative, antispasmodic, antidiarrheal, antiemetic, and carminative agent. However, its potential beneficial effects on intestinal and systemic changes induced by acute stress have not been fully elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: To assess the effects of its aqueous extract on the gastrointestinal system in a rat model of acute restraint stress related to inflammatory intestinal pathologies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Animals were treated for four consecutive days (n=6 per group) with Mv extract (250 and 500 mg/Kg p.o), clonazepam (1 mg/Kg p.o) or water. The acute stress model was induced by restraint for 6 hours in plastic cones adapted to the animal one hour after the last dose of the treatments. Control animals were not subjected to stress. Following the restraint period, animals were removed from the plastic cone and weighed. Glycemia and corticosterone were determined in plasma. Histological analysis and inflammatory and permeability markers were measured in colon and ileum samples. RESULTS: Stressed animals exhibited elevated corticosterone levels and intestinal damage, including villous rupture, goblet cell depletion, and increased biogenic amines levels. Treatment with Mv extract prevented these alterations in the ileum and colon and improved short-chain fatty acid profiles, especially butyrate and acetate in the colon. Stress also increased the glutathione redox ratio, upregulated inflammatory markers (TNFα, IL-1β, IL-6, TGFβ) and PI3K/AKT pathway proteins in the colon, effects that were attenuated by the extract. Furthermore, markers associated with cytoskeletal uncoupling (pVASP) and extracellular matrix remodeling (MMP-2) were reduced by Mv, suggesting a protective effect against stress-induced mucosal structural and molecular alterations. No changes were observed in myeloperoxidase activity, indicating that neutrophils were likely not involved in the observed inflammatory response. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates, for the first time, the ability of Mv to reduce the imbalance induced by acute restraint stress. Mitigation of inflammatory cascades, preservation of goblet cell lineage, attenuation of markers associated with cytoskeletal uncoupling (pVASP) and extracellular matrix remodeling (MMP-2) markers, and maintenance of colonic short-chain fatty acids represent key protective mechanisms. These findings suggest that Mv could exert beneficial effects in stress-related intestinal disorders.

articles.title: Artepillin C from Artemisia capillaris attenuates liver fibrosis by targeting NR3C2 and regulating the PPAR-γ/Smad axis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Artemisia capillaris is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb and widely used for the treatment of jaundice, hepatitis, and other liver-related diseases. Contemporary pharmacological studies have revealed its hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic activities. However, the bioactive constituents responsible for its anti-hepatic fibrotic effect remain poorly defined. Artepillin C (AC), one of the coumaric acid derivatives isolated from A. capillaris, has not yet been studied in liver fibrosis, and its mechanism of action is still unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the anti-hepatic fibrotic effects of AC in vitro and in vivo, and to elucidate its molecular target and underlying mechanism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The anti-fibrotic activity of AC was assessed in transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-induced hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation models using LX-2 and JS-1 cells, and validated in a carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis. The expression of extracellular matrix (ECM)-related markers were analyzed by Western blot, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence (IF). Transcriptomic analysis, target prediction and experimental screening were introduced to identify potential molecular targets of AC. The interaction between AC and target was validated by molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, which were supported by the cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS). Receptor agonist/antagonist treatment, and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) were conducted to explore the anti-fibrotic mechanism of AC. RESULTS: AC markedly attenuated TGF-β1-induced activation of HSCs without apparent cytotoxicity and reduced the expression of ECM proteins, including fibronectin (FN) and collagen I. In CCl4-induced mice, AC alleviated liver injury and reduced ECM deposition. Transcriptomic analysis combined with target prediction suggested that nuclear receptor subfamily 3 group C member 2 (NR3C2) was a potential target of AC. Docking and MD simulation indicated that AC could interact with NR3C2, while the CETSA and DARTS further demonstrated that AC binds to NR3C2 and increases its resistance to thermal denaturation and protease digestion. Mechanistically, AC downregulated NR3C2 expression, weakened the interaction between NR3C2 and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ), and restored PPAR-γ levels at higher concentrations, thereby suppressing TGF-β1-induced Smad2/3 phosphorylation. Consistent with these results, activation of NR3C2 enhanced Smad2/3 phosphorylation, whereas inhibition of NR3C2 or PPAR-γ attenuated Smad2/3 phosphorylation. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that AC, a natural product derived from A. capillaris, attenuates liver fibrosis by targeting NR3C2 and regulating the PPAR-γ/Smad axis. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the anti-fibrotic effects of AC and further expand the pharmacological understanding of A. capillaris-derived bioactive constituents.

articles.title: Changma Xifeng Tablet alleviates Tourette syndrome by restoring striatal dopaminergic homeostasis via the C1qa/TLR4-mediated microglial polarization.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The traditional botanical formulation Changma Xifeng (CMXF), primarily composed of the rhizomes of Gastrodia elata Blume and the roots of Paeonia lactiflora Pall., has been historically utilized in ethnomedicine to treat involuntary muscle spasms and hyperactive motor anomalies. It has shown therapeutic potential in preclinical models of Tourette syndrome (TS). AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Changma Xifeng Tablet (CMXF) in a 3,3-iminodipropionitrile (IDPN)-induced Tourette syndrome-like rat model and to explore whether C1qa-associated neuroimmune changes are associated with CMXF treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were intraperitoneally injected with IDPN (350 mg/kg/day) for 7 consecutive days to establish a TS model. Rats were randomly divided into seven groups (n = 10 each): Control, CMXF-only, TS model, CMXF-L (78 mg/kg), CMXF-M (156 mg/kg), CMXF-H (312 mg/kg), and Tiapride (21 mg/kg). CMXF was administered orally once daily for 4 weeks. Behavioral assessments (stereotyped scores), histopathology (H&E and Nissl), striatal proteomics, Western blot, ELISA, and immunofluorescence were performed to evaluate therapeutic effects and mechanisms. RESULTS: CMXF significantly ameliorated tic-like stereotyped behaviors, reducing stereotyped scores by 51% versus the TS group (p < 0.001), and improved monoamine disturbances in TS rats. Specifically, compared with the Control group, TS rats exhibited increased striatal DA and NE levels (70.4 vs. 33.9 and 0.589 vs. 0.208, respectively), together with decreased brainstem 5-HT and striatal HVA levels (4.57 vs. 10.7 and 16.84 vs. 24.14, respectively), whereas CMXF-H markedly reversed these abnormalities, reducing striatal DA and NE to 39.3 and 0.288 and increasing brainstem 5-HT and striatal HVA to 8.81 and 24.34, respectively. CMXF-H also attenuated TS-associated alterations in striatal dopamine-related signaling, reducing the elevated expression of DRD1 and DRD2 by 61% and 15%, respectively, while increasing the reduced expression of COMT and MAO-B by 43% and 46%, respectively (p < 0.05 or p < 0.01). Proteomic profiling highlighted the classical complement cascade as a candidate pathway associated with CMXF treatment. Further analyses showed that CMXF treatment was associated with a 20% reduction in C1qa upregulation and decreased C1qa deposition on activated microglia (p < 0.05). CMXF treatment was also associated with attenuation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway and changes in microglia-associated markers, characterized by a 30% decrease in iNOS and a 47% increase in Arg-1 (p < 0.01). These changes coincided with reduced striatal neuroinflammation, with TNF-α and IL-1β decreasing by 21% and 46%, respectively (p < 0.01 or p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies C1qa-associated neuroinflammatory changes as a molecular feature of the IDPN-induced TS-like rat model and a candidate pathway associated with CMXF treatment. CMXF treatment was associated with reduced C1qa expression, attenuation of TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-related signaling, changes in M1/M2-associated microglial markers, and improvement in monoamine-related alterations. These findings suggest a potential relationship between C1qa-associated neuroinflammatory changes and the pharmacological effects of CMXF, while the causal role of C1qa remains to be determined.

articles.title: Da Chuanxiong extract modulates the Lands cycle to elicit spatially specific phospholipid remodeling against cerebral ischemia.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Da Chuanxiong (DCX), composed of Ligusticum chuanxiong Hort. and Gastrodia elata Bl. (4:1), is a classical Chinese herbal formula, traditionally used for headache and vertigo caused by wind pathogen and blood stasis. Modern clinical practice has extended its application to ischemic stroke. However, whether DCX exerts neuroprotection through Lands cycle-mediated phospholipid remodeling, particularly in a spatially specific manner, remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To demonstrate whether DCX elicits spatially specific phospholipid remodeling through Lands cycle activation, and to identify the brain-penetrating constituents responsible for this effect. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Protective effects of DCX were evaluated in pMCAO rats, and those of its brain-penetrating constituents were assessed in OGD/R-induced HT22 cells. Glycerophospholipid composition and spatial distribution were analyzed by targeted lipidomics and AFADESI-QQQ-MSI-based spatial metabolomics. Lands cycle enzyme expression was measured by RT-qPCR and western blotting. RESULTS: DCX dose-dependently reduced infarct volume and attenuated neuronal damage, accompanied by decreased ROS and MDA, elevated GSH, and preserved mitochondrial membrane integrity. Lipidomic analysis revealed that DCX shifted phospholipids from peroxidation-prone PUFA-PLs to oxidation-resistant SFA/MUFA-PLs in a spatially specific manner, reducing PUFA-PLs from 90.7% to 82.9% and increasing SFA/MUFA-PLs from 9.3% to 17.1%. SFA-PLs were region-selectively restored in hippocampus and thalamus, and MUFA-PLs in the corpus callosum and internal capsule. Mechanistically, DCX concurrently upregulated PLA2G6, ACSL3, MBOAT2, and LPCAT1, consistent with Lands cycle-mediated deacylation and reacylation. Five brain-penetrating constituents (senkyunolide A, butylphthalide, levistilide A, ferulic acid, and gastrodin) modulated these enzymes in vitro. CONCLUSION: This work provides the first evidence that DCX elicits spatially specific phospholipid remodeling toward oxidation-resistant species, an effect associated with Lands cycle activation and its brain-penetrating constituents. This remodeling may reduce peroxidation substrate availability and counteract lipid peroxidation in cerebral ischemia.

articles.title: Early PEG-bHb resuscitation for hemorrhagic shock: Attenuation of acute kidney injury via the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic shock (HS) is a major cause of traumatic death, strongly influenced by resuscitation timing. This study explored the protective effects and mechanisms of early polyethylene glycol-conjugated bovine hemoglobin (PEG-bHb) resuscitation in HS treatment. METHODS: Following subjecting HS, rats received PEG-bHb resuscitation at 0-30 min (R_30), 30-60 min (R_60), or 60-90 min (R_90), or conventional crystalloid-colloid solution as control. Hemodynamic, acid-base, and microcirculatory parameters, survival time, renal histopathology, and pimonidazole hypoxia staining were assessed to verify the resuscitation effect. Renal transcriptomic profiling was performed, followed by validation of inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, mitochondrial morphology, and Nrf2/HO-1 pathway activation. The Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 was used to confirm pathway involvement. RESULTS: All PEG-bHb groups showed restoration of hemodynamic, acid-base, and microcirculatory parameters, yet R_30 and R_60 significantly prolonged survival (27.59 h, 28.03 h) versus HES (<4 h). Histopathological and pimonidazole hypoxia staining showed markedly attenuated renal injury and reduced renal tissue hypoxia after early resuscitation. Transcriptomic and validation results revealed that R_30 suppressed renal inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis, restored mitochondrial morphology, and activated the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. Nrf2 inhibition by ML385 abolished these protective effects. CONCLUSIONS: Early PEG-bHb resuscitation ameliorates HS-induced acute kidney injury and improves survival by activating the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway.

articles.title: Bergenin attenuates diabetic cardiomyopathy by inhibiting oxidative stress and ferroptosis through modulation of the YAP signaling axis.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Diabetes mellitus-associated cardiac dysfunction arises from metabolic imbalance, oxidative stress, inflammation, maladaptive remodeling, and impaired cardiac performance. Bergenin (BER), a naturally occurring small molecule with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory properties, has shown therapeutic potential; however, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains unclear. This study investigated the cardioprotective effects of BER in DCM, with particular emphasis on oxidative stress, the Hippo-Yes-associated protein (YAP), and ferroptosis signaling axis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: DCM was induced in rats using a high-fat diet combined with low-dose streptozotocin (STZ). Diabetic rats received BER (25 or 50 mg/kg/day) or empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day). Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography, followed by histopathological and molecular analyses. To further investigate the underlying mechanisms, H9c2 cardiomyoblasts exposed to high glucose were used for in vitro assessment of oxidative stress, Hippo-YAP signaling, and ferroptosis-related markers. KEY FINDINGS: In vivo, BER treatment significantly improved cardiac function, attenuated histopathological injury, and reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and fibrosis in diabetic rats. Consistent with these findings, in vitro, BER reduced reactive oxygen species generation, restored mitochondrial integrity, and prevented high glucose-induced injury in H9c2 cells. Mechanistically, BER modulated YAP signaling and suppressed ferroptosis-related changes. YAP silencing attenuated the protective effects of BER, supporting a critical role for YAP in mediating its anti-ferroptotic effects. SIGNIFICANCE: These findings demonstrate that BER exerts cardioprotective effects against diabetes-associated cardiac dysfunction and provide mechanistic evidence implicating the YAP-ferroptosis axis in this protection. Further studies are warranted to establish its translational potential.

articles.title: Artesunate targets STAT3 to alleviate Hodgkin's lymphoma via JAK-STAT/PD-L1 axis.
articles.abstract: Relapsed or refractory Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is resistant to existing chemotherapy and PD-1 inhibitors, creating an urgent need for safe and effective drugs with novel mechanisms of action. Artesunate (ART), a classic antimalarial agent, has recently demonstrated broad-spectrum antitumor activity. However, its direct targets and core molecular mechanisms in HL remain unclear. In this study, we combined HuProt™ 20 K human proteome microarray, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro functional assays to identify the key targets and signaling pathways of ART against HL. Critical functional residues were validated through site-directed mutagenesis. Proteome microarray and protein-protein interaction network analysis identified STAT3 as the core target of ART in HL. Molecular docking revealed a binding energy of -7.2 kcal/mol between ART and STAT3, with Glu638 identified as a critical interacting residue. Functional experiments confirmed that ART significantly inhibited STAT3 phosphorylation, reduced the levels of soluble PD-L1, BCL-XL, and IL-6 in the supernatant, and suppressed HL cell proliferation and migration. Notably, both the STAT3E638A mutation and STAT3-siRNA completely abolished the antitumor effects of ART. Collectively, ART blocks the JAK-STAT/PD-L1 signaling axis by targeting Glu638 of STAT3, achieving dual effects of inhibiting tumor survival and reversing immune evasion. This work identifies STAT3 as a direct binding target of ART in HL and establishes Glu638 as a critical functional site, providing a robust theoretical and experimental foundation for repurposing ART in the treatment of relapsed or refractory HL.

articles.title: Influence of dietary protein deficiency on the progression and resolution of CCl₄-induced liver damage.
articles.abstract: Malnutrition remains a major global health challenge and is associated with increased susceptibility to liver disease and impaired recovery following hepatic injury. This research assesses the impact of a low-protein diet (LPD) on mice subjected to carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄)-induced liver damage. How an established state of protein deficiency affects the temporal progression of liver injury and the subsequent process of hepatic recovery remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study investigated the influence of long-term dietary protein-deficiency on the progression and resolution of CCl₄-induced liver injury using a longitudinal experimental approach. A preliminary dose-selection study identified 2 mL/kg CCl₄ as the optimal dose in both dietary groups-normal diet (ND) and LPD. The time course of injury due to CCl₄ post-administration was assessed at 0-72 h. Injury was apparent by 1 h, reached a maximum at 24 h, and was more significant in the LPD group compared to the ND group. By 72 h, ND mice showed near-complete recovery, whereas liver injury persisted in LPD mice. Inflammatory markers (TNF-α and IL-6) indicated greater inflammatory responses in the LPD mice. Also, elevated PCNA and MDA levels in the LPD mice suggest that there was increased oxidative stress in addition to an increased compensatory cell proliferation response. Histopathological assessment revealed more extensive tissue damage, including necrosis, apoptosis, and delayed regenerative recovery, in LPD mice. Therefore, by defining the temporal pattern of liver injury and recovery, this study provides a framework for identifying optimal intervention windows and evaluating therapeutic strategies under protein-deficiency conditions.

articles.title: Albumin/BSH-fused nanoparticle for boron neutron capture therapy of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive malignant tumor which suffers from poor prognosis and limited therapeutic remedies. As a physiologically-oriented radiotherapy and highly tumor-specific modality, boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) shows great potential for the treatment of ESCC. Since efficacy of BNCT is critically restricted to boron drugs, novel boron agents with satisfactory boron load and intracellular uptake are highly demanded. Herein, we developed a novel albumin/BSH-conjugated nanoparticle (BSH@Alb) as a safe and effective boron agent. It resulted BSH@Alb displayed uniform particle size, high encapsulation efficiency (93.1 ± 0.39%), loading capacity (15.52 ± 0.41%) and good stability in different solution (water, PBS and plasma). Collectively, BSH@Alb significantly enhanced intracellular boron accumulation and showed acceptable cytocompatibility in comparison with prototype BSH, supporting its potential value for BNCT therapy as a promising boron-delivery candidate.

articles.title: Nicotinate Phosphoribosyltransferase controls aggressiveness, Ca2+ homeostasis, and NAD+-derived Ca2+ mobilizing second messengers in triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) represents the most aggressive form of breast cancer (BC), being characterized by a high metastatic rate and a poor prognosis due to its tendency to relapse and the lack of targeted therapies. Inhibition of NAD+ synthesis, mostly by targeting Nicotinamide Phosphoribosyltransferase in the salvage pathway, showed promise as anticancer therapy, as NAD+ is implicated in tumor growth, energy production, motion and invasiveness, immune response, and multi-drug resistance. We investigated the role of Nicotinate Phosphoribosyltransferase (NAPRT), the rate-limiting enzyme for NAD+ synthesis starting from nicotinate, in TNBC proliferation, invasiveness, also through the use of a 3D culture model, and in Ca2+ homeostasis. Our results demonstrated that NAPRT promotes tumor aggression and determines the concomitant increase of the cytosolic Ca2+ levels and the decrease in state of replenishment of Thapsigargin-sensitive ER Ca2+ stores. Also, NAPRT overexpression increased the levels of the Ca2+-mobilizing messengers cyclic ADPR and Nicotinic Acid Adenine Dinucleotide Phosphate (measurements with a newly developed assay) and the pharmacological CD38 or SARM1 inhibition reverted the NAPRT-induced changes in Ca2+ homeostasis. Therefore, targeting NAPRT may represent a promising strategy to slow down TNBC growth and progression.

articles.title: Preventing oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy with a Pt(IV)-Mn(II) prodrug: Toxicity, behavioral and X-ray fluorescence microscopy studies.
articles.abstract: Although widely used in chemotherapeutic treatments, platinum (Pt)-based drugs -namely cisplatin (Cis), oxaliplatin (Ox), and carboplatin- encounter several drawbacks that significantly limit their clinically applicable doses, such as the development of various side effects. These toxicities, including nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity associated with Cis and Ox, respectively, arise from the lack of selectivity of these drugs toward cancer cells. While numerous alternative treatments -some employing a Pt(IV) prodrug strategy- have been investigated in preclinical settings for their anticancer activity, studies evaluating their systemic toxicities remain scarce. However, assessing these toxicities is crucial for the development of improved therapies. This study aimed to evaluate the systemic toxicities induced by PtC5Mn, a novel Pt(IV)-Mn(II) prodrug reported to exhibit anticancer activity in both in vitro and in vivo models of colorectal cancer, as well as Mn1C5, its corresponding Mn(II) complex that mimics superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, in combination with Ox. Additionally, their potential protective effects against Ox-induced peripheral neuropathy were explored through behavioral studies and mapping of Pt localization in sciatic nerves sections by Synchrotron-based Scanning X-Ray Fluorescence microscopy. Our results support the use of Pt(IV) prodrugs and redox modulation by SOD mimics for the mitigation of oxaliplatin-associated off-target effects.

articles.title: Jiedu Quyu Ziyin Decoction attenuates high-phosphate-induced calcification-associated phenotypes in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells.
articles.abstract: Vascular calcification is one of the complications related to chronic kidney disease, and there are correlations between vascular calcification and oxidative stress, inflammation, and ferroptosis. This study examined whether Jiedu Quyu Ziyin Decoction (JQZYD) attenuates high-phosphate-induced calcification in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells and evaluated the contribution of NRF2-associated antioxidant signalling. Human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells were exposed to high-phosphate conditions and treated with JQZYD. Calcification was assessed by Alizarin Red S staining, calcium content, alkaline phosphatase activity, and osteogenic markers. Ferroptosis-associated changes were evaluated by BODIPY 581/591 C11 oxidation, intracellular Fe2⁺, glutathione, glutathione peroxidase activity, and GPX4/SLC7A11 expression. NRF2 activation was assessed by immunofluorescence and protein analysis. Ferrostatin-1, RSL3, and NFE2L2 silencing were used for mechanistic evaluation. Inflammatory mediators and conditioned-medium effects were also examined. JQZYD reduced high-phosphate-induced mineral deposition, osteogenic marker expression, lipid peroxidation, Fe2⁺ accumulation, and inflammatory responses. These changes were accompanied by increased glutathione peroxidase activity, greater NRF2 nuclear accumulation, higher GPX4 and SLC7A11 transcript abundance, and increased NRF2 and GPX4 protein abundance. Ferrostatin-1 reproduced several protective effects of JQZYD. RSL3 and NFE2L2 silencing partially attenuated JQZYD-associated protection, supporting contributions of GPX4-related lipid peroxide regulation and NRF2-associated signalling without establishing direct NRF2 regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4 or pathway order. Conditioned medium from JQZYD-treated donor cells induced weaker inflammatory and calcific responses in recipient HASMCs, although the responsible mediators and potential contribution of residual treatment components remained unresolved. JQZYD attenuated high-phosphate-induced calcification-associated phenotypes and accompanying oxidative and inflammatory responses in cultured HASMCs. NFE2L2 silencing supports NRF2 involvement without establishing direct regulation of SLC7A11/GPX4 or pathway order. These findings are restricted to a cellular model and do not establish prevention of vascular calcification or therapeutic efficacy in CKD. Validation in CKD-relevant animal models and more physiologically complex vascular systems is required.

articles.title: Desethylhydroxychloroquine and CYP2D6 polymorphisms are associated with low disease activity in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is standard therapy for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), but the clinical relevance of its active metabolite, desethylhydroxychloroquine (DHCQ), remains unclear. We examined whether DHCQ exposure is more closely related to disease control than HCQ exposure in Japanese patients with SLE. METHODS: Patients receiving HCQ for at least 6 months were enrolled. Whole-blood and plasma HCQ and DHCQ, and plasma 4β-hydroxycholesterol (a CYP3A activity marker), were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and CYP2D6 (*2, *5, *10) and CYP3A5 (*3) were genotyped. The primary outcome was low disease activity (LDA), defined as SLEDAI-2K ≤ 4 with oral corticosteroids ≤5 mg/day. Exposures were analysed as continuous variables (log-transformed, per 1 SD) in multivariable logistic regression; cutoff-based analyses were exploratory, with optimism assessed by bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: Among 102 patients, 36 (35.3%) attained LDA. The 23 (22.5%) CYP2D6 intermediate metabolisers had lower DHCQ/HCQ ratios and weight-adjusted DHCQ concentration-to-dose ratios than normal metabolisers in both matrices. HCQ concentrations and CYP genotypes were not associated with LDA. Adjusted odds ratios per 1 SD increase were 1.80 (95% CI 1.10-2.95) for plasma DHCQ, 2.10 (1.23-3.59) for the plasma DHCQ/HCQ ratio, 1.73 (1.04-2.88) for whole-blood DHCQ and 2.36 (1.32-4.23) for the whole-blood DHCQ/HCQ ratio. Discrimination was modest (AUC 0.62-0.67; lower bootstrap limits 0.50-0.56). CONCLUSIONS: CYP2D6 genotype was the principal determinant of DHCQ exposure. Higher DHCQ concentrations and DHCQ/HCQ ratios, but not HCQ concentrations or genotypes, were associated with LDA, supporting DHCQ as a candidate exposure marker requiring prospective validation.

articles.title: Availability and reimbursement of fixed-dose combination medicines for hypertension treatment in Central and Eastern Europe.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Fixed-dose combinations (FDCs) represent an important strategy in modern pharmacotherapy and are particularly beneficial in the treatment of chronic conditions such as hypertension because they reduce pill burden and may improve patient adherence to therapy. OBJECTIVES: The primary objective of this study was to compare reimbursement, pricing, and availability policies for FDC medicines used in the treatment of arterial hypertension across 15 CEE countries. Additionally, the study aimed to assess differences in HTA requirements and patient co-payments among the analyzed countries. METHODS: Data were collected from the reimbursement systems of 15 CEE countries using a questionnaire distributed to native experts in each country to ensure contextual accuracy. The list of potential active substance combinations was derived from established clinical guidelines. Associations were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficients and generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs). RESULTS: Substantial variation in reimbursement requirements was observed across CEE countries. The greatest variability concerned the inclusion of adherence and persistence outcomes in reimbursement decision-making processes. Seven countries considered these aspects in their reimbursement assessments, whereas the remaining countries did not. The four most frequently reimbursed two-component FDCs were combinations of ARBs with CCBs, ACEIs with CCBs, ACEIs with diuretics, and ARBs with diuretics. Public pharmaceutical expenditure related to hypertension treatment varied substantially across countries; with Estonia allocating the highest proportion of hypertension reimbursement expenditure to FDCs (68% in 2022). The time required for inclusion on reimbursement lists also differed markedly, ranging from less than 3 months in Latvia and Lithuania to more than 12 months in Albania and Romania. Spearman correlation analyses demonstrated that the total number of reimbursed FDCs in a given country was significantly associated with HTA requirements for FDCs containing previously reimbursed components (ρ = 0.641, p = 0.011) and with the time from reimbursement application to inclusion on the reimbursement list (ρ = -0.548, p = 0.041). Multivariable GLMM analysis confirmed that: i) countries with less stringent requirements for FDCs containing already reimbursed components (i.e., countries that either do not require an HTA assessment or make the HTA requirement contingent on the manufacturer's proposed price) had a significantly higher number of reimbursed FDCs (p = 0.001); and ii) countries with less stringent HTA requirements for FDCs (i.e., those that do not require additional comparators beyond the individual FDC components) also tended to have a higher number of reimbursed FDCs (p = 0.010). CONCLUSION: Across CEE countries, less burdensome HTA and reimbursement requirements for FDCs composed of already known and reimbursed active substances were associated with broader reimbursement of single-pill antihypertensive therapies. Streamlining assessment pathways for well-justified, guideline-supported combinations could improve patient access and better align reimbursement practice with current clinical guidelines, while preserving evidence-based decision-making. Common EU-level clinical assessment processes may further support consistency across national HTA systems, although pricing and reimbursement decisions remain within national competence.

articles.title: Gypenoside LI modulates autophagy-associated apoptosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma by PPARG/PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR/ULK1 signaling network.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study was conducted to comprehensively evaluate the anti-clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) activity of gypenoside LI (Gyp LI) through in vitro and in vivo models; elucidate the specific molecular pathways mediating the induction of apoptosis and autophagy in Gyp LI-treated ccRCC cells, focusing on the regulatory role of Gypenoside LI in upregulating PPARG and coordinately modulating the PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR-ULK1 signaling network; and render experimental evidence and theoretical support to develop Gyp LI as a novel anti-ccRCC agent. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Human ccRCC cell lines (769-P and ACHN) and a BALB/c nude mouse xenograft model were used for this study. The suppressive effect of Gyp LI on ccRCC cell proliferation was assessed by colony formation assay, Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay, wound healing assay, and Hoechst staining. Autophagy-related ultrastructural changes in treated cells were observed by transmission electron microscopy. Western blot and quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) were conducted to evaluate fluctuations in the expression levels of autophagic and apoptotic process markers. Putative therapeutic targets associated with Gyp LI were predicted utilizing a network pharmacology framework. Concurrently, the transcriptional control exerted by PPARG over the PTEN gene was validated by dual-luciferase reporter systems and chromatin immunoprecipitation combined with quantitative PCR. To clarify the regulatory relationships within the signaling pathway, we performed in vitro rescue experiments using target gene knockdown. Additionally, a subcutaneous xenograft model in nude mice was established for assessing the in vivo antitumor activity and biosafety of Gyp LI. Apoptosis-, autophagy-, and pathway-related protein expression in tumor tissues was assessed by Western blotting (WB) assay. RESULTS: CCK-8 reagent-based cell viability assay revealed that Gyp LI dose-dependently inhibited 769-P and ACHN cell growth, with 24-h IC50 values of 62.57 and 79.30 μM, respectively. Colony formation, wound healing, and Hoechst staining assay results collectively showed that Gyp LI suppressed cell proliferation and migration and exerted apoptotic effects. Morphological and molecular assays showed that Gyp LI-treated ccRCC cells exhibited prominent autophagosomes and autolysosomes, with upregulation of the autophagy-related proteins Beclin1, ATG5, and LC3 I/II and downregulation of P62. The antiapoptotic factor Bcl-2 exhibited substantially reduced expression, while the proapoptotic mediators caspase-3 and Bax were upregulated, these findings indicated concurrent autophagy-related alterations and apoptosis in Gyp LI-treated ccRCC cells. WB and RT-qPCR assays revealed that Gyp LI upregulated the mRNA and protein expression of the transcription factor PPARG. PTEN transcription was stimulated by the specific binding of PPARG to its promoter region. The resulting intracellular accumulation of PTEN effectively blocked abnormal activation associated with the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling axis and ultimately modulated autophagy-associated apoptosis through the phosphorylation-mediated activation of ULK1. ULK1 knockdown reversed the autophagic phenotype modulated by Gyp LI. Moreover, PPARG knockdown reversed Gyp LI-mediated PTEN upregulation, PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway inhibition, and ULK1 phosphorylation, while attenuating Gyp LI-modulated autophagy and apoptosis. In vivo experiments showed that oral administration of Gyp LI significantly inhibited xenograft tumor growth but did not affect body weight in nude mice. WB assay further confirmed increased expression of proapoptotic and autophagy-related proteins and decreased expression of phosphorylated AKT/mTOR pathway proteins in Gyp LI-treated tumor tissues. However, further studies are required to fully elucidate the autophagic flux and the direct binding targets. CONCLUSION: This study revealed that Gyp LI promotes cell death associated with autophagic alterations in ccRCC cell lines. Mechanistically, this phenomenon is driven by upregulating PPARG and coordinately modulating the PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR-ULK1 signaling network, but the exact causal interdependencies and comprehensive biosafety profile warrant further investigation before any clinical translation. The in vivo efficacy suggests that Gyp LI could serve as promising candidates for plant-derived therapeutic interventions for treating RCC.

articles.title: Influence of dietary supplementation with French maritime pine bark extract (Pycnogenol®) on endothelial glycocalyx structures in a dynamic cell culture model.
articles.abstract: The endothelial glycocalyx (GCX) is a major contributor to endothelial cell function and vascular integrity. GCX damage has been linked to atherosclerosis promotion and other pathophysiologic states. The dietary supplement Pycnogenol®, a standardized extract from the bark of Pinus pinaster, has shown beneficial impact on cardiovascular and endothelial health in various clinical studies, but the underlying effect mechanism is not fully understood. The purpose of the present investigation was to explore the influence of human serum collected before and after Pycnogenol® supplementation on the properties of the endothelial GCX under basal, osmotic and inflammatory conditions. Since static cell culture poorly reproduces a physiologically relevant GCX, while controlled flow systems are technically demanding, a suitable cell culture model was to be established. A dynamic culture model using a rocking shaker was successfully implemented. Visualization of endothelial GCX structures using lectin-based staining with wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) revealed significantly increased WGA intensity (approximately 60%) under dynamic compared to static culture conditions. Under dynamic conditions, endothelial cell viability and proliferation were significantly enhanced as well as the functional responsiveness to TNF-alpha and sodium chloride exposure. When cells were dynamically incubated with serum samples obtained from healthy volunteers before and after intake of Pycnogenol®, the WGA signal intensity per cell significantly increased across all conditions. Endothelial monolayer permeability as determined with labelled dextran decreased by up to 48% after incubation with serum obtained after intake of Pycnogenol®. Moreover, the GCX shedding markers syndecan-4 and hyaluronan were significantly lower after supplementation with a significant attenuation of the response to TNF-alpha, suggesting a potential GCX protective effect by Pycnogenol® under inflammatory conditions. In summary, this study demonstrated that dynamic culture conditions promoted the formation of more pronounced glycocalyx-associated surface structures in human endothelial cells compared to static culture. In the dynamic cell culture model, application of serum samples obtained after intake of Pycnogenol® was associated with improvement of endothelial GCX properties suggesting that bioavailable and bioactive Pycnogenol® constituents and/or metabolites stabilized the endothelial GCX and improved barrier integrity.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of antifibrotic activity of Salvadora persica extracts in CCl4-induced liver fibrosis in rats by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation via transcriptional modulation associated with TGF-β1/Smad signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Plant Salvadora persica (SP) is well-known for its pharmacological activities, including its role in oral hygiene. In the present study, we investigated, the in vivo comparative hepatoprotective potential of SP root extracts against chronic liver injury fibrosis. In Wistar albino rats, liver fibrosis was induced by intraperitoneal injection of carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) in olive oil (1:1 v/v) at 1 mL/kg, twice weekly for 9 weeks. Liver damage was evaluated by measuring serum liver biochemical parameters, antioxidant enzyme levels, and lipid peroxidation marker in liver homogenate. The mRNA expression level of inflammatory and profibrotic markers in liver tissue and histopathology of liver tissue by H&E staining and collagen deposition by Masson's trichrome, and Van Gieson's staining were determined. SP extracts, including aqueous (SP-AQ), ethanolic (SP-E), and petroleum ether (SP-PE), were analyzed by Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS), followed by multivariate principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA). The findings demonstrated that SP extracts demonstrated significant hepatoprotective effects by improving rats' body weight without significant increase in liver index, reducing liver biochemical markers, and reducing oxidative stress by increasing SOD and GPx levels and decreasing MDA level. In liver tissue, the mRNA expression levels of the inflammatory markers IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α and profibrotic markers TGF-β1, Smad2, Smad3, α-SMA, and Collagen1A1 were downregulated by modulating the genes expression levels related with the TGF-β1/Smad signaling pathway. Histopathology showed recovery from liver damage and reduced collagen deposition. Comparatively, antifibrotic activity was greater by SP-PE, modest by SP-E and lowest by SP-AQ extracts. Furthermore, phytochemical analysis of the SP extracts demonstrated considerable diversity in their phytoconstituent profiles due to difference in solvent polarity, with PCA and PLS-DA analyses confirming distinct clustering and discrimination among SP extracts. SP-PE extract, greater efficacy can be attributed to selection of a non-polar solvent and 4-propenyl-2,6-dimethoxyphenol, along with other dominant phytochemicals, which exerted synergistic biological effects. The SP extracts showed significant hepatoprotective activity with consistent biological effects in reducing oxidative stress, inflammation, and fibrosis in CCl4-induced liver fibrosis in rats. However, further studies of major individual compounds of SP-PE are warranted for clinical use in liver fibrosis.

articles.title: Multi-omics integration reveals the role of PFOS in sarcopenia via ESRRG and RBP4: from computational prediction to experimental validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) has been shown to cause multi-organ dysfunction; however, the specific mechanisms underlying its association with sarcopenia remain unclear. METHODS: Network toxicology analysis was performed to identify potential molecular targets and related signaling pathways involved in PFOS-induced sarcopenia. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations further screened stable PFOS-target interactions. Single-nucleus RNA-seq analysis was used to assess cell-type-specific PFOS-related signatures and ESRRG/RBP4-associated regulatory pathways in skeletal muscle. Finally, in vitro experiments were performed to evaluate the effects of PFOS on myogenic differentiation. RESULTS: Network toxicology identified seven potential targets enriched in the PPAR signaling pathway. Molecular simulations indicated stable binding interactions between PFOS and ESRRG/RBP4. Single-nucleus RNA-seq analysis suggested that mast cells may represent a potential PFOS-responsive cell population and revealed cytoskeleton-related pathway alterations associated with ESRRG and RBP4. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that PFOS markedly inhibited myogenic differentiation, accompanied by downregulation of related protein expression. CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates that exposure to PFOS is associated with an increased risk of sarcopenia and identifies ESRRG and RBP4 as key mediators of PFOS-associated myotoxicity.

articles.title: Evaluation of the anticancer effects of kaempferol using in vitro assays and [99mTc]Tc-PSMA SPECT/CT imaging in a DMBA-induced breast cancer model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Kaempferol is a naturally occurring flavonoid with reported anticancer properties; however, its effects on breast cancer cells and tumor-associated molecular imaging require further investigation. This study evaluated the effects of kaempferol using complementary in vitro assays and a 7,12-dimethylbenz [a]anthracene (DMBA)-induced breast cancer rat model assessed by [99mTc]Tc-PSMA SPECT/CT imaging. METHODS: MCF-7 breast cancer cells were treated with kaempferol, and cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay across a concentration range of 0-80 µM. Apoptosis, wound closure, and the expression of E-cadherin and VEGF were also evaluated. The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) was estimated using nonlinear four-parameter logistic regression of replicate-level concentration-response data. In vivo, 8-week-old rats were allocated into cancer control, kaempferol pre-treatment, and post-treatment groups (n = 10/group). Mammary tumors were induced using DMBA, and animals received kaempferol (100 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) according to the experimental protocol. Tumor-associated tracer uptake was evaluated using [99mTc]Tc-PSMA SPECT/CT imaging and quantified using tumor-to-background ratios (TBRs). RESULTS: Kaempferol reduced MCF-7 cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner, with nonlinear regression estimating an IC50 of approximately 40 µM. Kaempferol treatment was associated with increased apoptosis, reduced wound closure, increased E-cadherin expression, and decreased VEGF expression.
