In vivo imaging demonstrated significant differences in tumor tracer uptake among the experimental groups. The pre-treatment group showed significantly lower TBR values (64.65 ± 1.69) than the cancer control (71.18 ± 1.83) and post-treatment groups (71.16 ± 1.06), whereas no significant difference was observed between the cancer control and post-treatment groups. One-way ANOVA demonstrated a significant overall group effect (F (2,27) = 58.08, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.81). CONCLUSION: Kaempferol demonstrated concentration-dependent cytotoxic effects and modulation of cancer-associated cellular markers in MCF-7 cells. In the DMBA-induced breast cancer model, reduced tumor-associated [99mTc]Tc-PSMA uptake was observed predominantly following kaempferol pre-treatment, suggesting a potential chemopreventive effect. The findings support the complementary use of in vitro pharmacological assays and molecular imaging to investigate treatment-associated changes in tumor biology.

articles.title: Amomum tsao-ko volatile oil alleviates renal fibrosis in 5/6 nephrectomy rats through TGF-β1/SMAD3 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Renal fibrosis is the main cause of many kidney diseases and a common outcome of many chronic kidney diseases. The dried mature fruit of Amomum tsao-ko is widely used to treat various diseases, including those characterized by diuresis and detumescence. Amomum tsao-ko volatile oil (AO) may be the active ingredient responsible for its main pharmacological action, and its protective effect and mechanism in kidney injury models are unclear. Therefore, based on transcriptomics and animal experiments, this study discusses the mechanism of AO through TGF‑β1/SMAD3 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways in renal fibrosis of 5/6 nephrectomy rats. METHODS: Seventy-two healthy SD rats were randomly divided into 6 groups. The rat renal fibrosis model was established by 5/6 nephrectomy. Different doses of AO were given by gavage. After 28 days of continuous administration, the levels of creatinine and urea nitrogen in serum of rats were detected. The total RNA of rat kidney tissue was extracted for transcriptomics determination and analysis showed the expression of differential genes in each group. The core targets related to chronic kidney injury were docked with the main components of the AO. HE, PAS and Masson staining were used to observe the pathological morphology of renal tissue in rats. Western Blot was used to detect the expression of p-PI3K, PI3K, AKT, p-AKT, SMAD3, TGF-β1, MMP-9 and TIMP-1 in renal tissue. RESULTS: Compared with the Sham group, the transcriptome results showed that there were 823 genes with significant differences in expression; the levels of SCr and BUN in the model group were significantly increased. HE, PAS and Masson found that 5/6 Nx could develop interstitial fibrosis. At the same time, a large number of renal tubular epithelial cells were atrophied, deformed and exfoliated, and a large number of inflammatory cells infiltrated in the interstitium. Western Blot results showed that the expression of PI3 K, AKT, TIMP-1, SMAD3, TGF-β1 and other proteins in the 5/6 Nx group increased significantly, and the expression of MMP-9 protein decreased significantly. Compared with the 5/6 Nx group, there were 1,009 genes with significant differences in expression after treatment with AO, and the levels of SCr and BUN decreased. The infiltration of inflammatory cells in renal tissue was improved. The expression of PI3K, AKT, TIMP-1, SMAD3 and TGF-β1 was significantly decreased, and the expression of MMP-9 was significantly increased. CONCLUSION: AO can further inhibit the phosphorylation level by inhibiting the TGF- β1/SMAD3 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways in 5/6 Nx rats, thus effectively improving the pathological damage of renal tissue.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance analysis and cross-database consistency assessment of resmetirom-related adverse events using FAERS and VigiAccess.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the post-marketing safety profile and potential adverse event signals of resmetirom using the FAERS and VigiAccess databases. METHODS: FAERS reports from the quarter of initial United States approval through 2026Q1 were analyzed. After deduplication, DEMO, DRUG, REAC, THER, and OUTC tables were integrated, and reports listing resmetirom as the primary suspect drug were included. Disproportionality analysis used four methods: reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS), with IC and EBGM as the respective Bayesian signal metrics. PTs meeting all four predefined criteria were defined as robust signals. Additional analyses assessed SOC/PT profiles, label expectedness, seriousness and outcomes, time-to-onset (TTO), Weibull patterns, and cross-database consistency with VigiAccess. RESULTS: We identified 1,409 resmetirom-related FAERS reports and 1,417 VigiAccess reports. Sixty-two robust PT signals across nine SOCs were detected, mainly involving gastrointestinal disorders, investigations, hepatobiliary disorders, and skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders. Prominent signals included diarrhoea, nausea, pruritus, alanine aminotransferase increased, aspartate aminotransferase increased, abdominal pain upper, dizziness, vomiting, weight decreased, and hepatic cirrhosis. Among FAERS reports, 419 (29.7%) were serious and 65 (4.6%) reported death. Sixteen robust PTs were not listed as corresponding adverse reactions in either the current United States. Prescribing Information or European SmPC. Complete temporal information was available for 170 reports (12.1%); median TTO was 26 days (IQR, 5-66), and the Weibull shape parameter was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.64-0.80), indicating an early-failure pattern. SOC-stratified analyses showed heterogeneous onset patterns. FAERS and VigiAccess showed high descriptive concordance in SOC- and PT-level reporting patterns (Spearman ρ = 0.998). CONCLUSION: Resmetirom-related reports were mainly gastrointestinal, laboratory, hepatobiliary, and skin-related. Hepatobiliary signals warrant particular attention, while cross-database concordance provides supportive, non-causal pharmacovigilance evidence.

articles.title: Multi-source data integration and ensemble machine learning analysis of the role of Corilagin in regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress and alleviating intestinal ischemia reperfusion injury in mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IIRI) is driven by oxidative stress, excessive inflammation, Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress (ERS), and disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier. Corilagin, a natural ellagitannin with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, has shown protective effects against IIRI; however, its cross-species and multitarget mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: This study investigated the protective mechanisms of Corilagin against IIRI by integrating Corilagin-related targets, IIRI-associated genes, and an ERS gene set. Differential expression analyses of GSE37013 and GSE96733 were combined with an ensemble machine-learning framework comprising 15 algorithms to prioritize core genes. Molecular docking and 100-ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations using the AlphaFold-predicted full-length human NRF2 structure were performed to assess the predicted Corilagin-NRF2 interaction. A mouse IIRI model was used to validate selected molecular and histological findings by histology, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. In IEC-6 cells subjected to OGD/R, NRF2 immunofluorescence and siRNA-mediated knockdown of Nrf2 or Abcg2 were used to further evaluate the involvement of NRF2 and ABCG2 in Corilagin-mediated protection. RESULTS: Intersection analysis identified 472 genes shared among Corilagin-related targets, IIRI-related genes, and ERS-associated genes. Enrichment analysis highlighted stress- and injury-related pathways, including PI3K-Akt signaling. Ensemble machine learning prioritized 12 core genes across human and mouse datasets, with ABCG2, IL10, and PRKCZ emerging as prominent candidates. Docking and 100-ns MD simulations supported persistent Corilagin retention within the predicted NRF2 binding region, while post-relaxation MM/GBSA analysis indicated favorable interaction energetics. In vivo, Corilagin pretreatment reduced inflammation and oxidative stress-related changes, restored apical ABCG2 and tight-junction protein expression, improved mucosal morphology, and altered CHOP expression. In IEC-6 cells, Nrf2 or Abcg2 knockdown weakened Corilagin-mediated preservation of Occludin, Claudin-1, and ZO-1 under OGD/R, supporting NRF2-ABCG2 involvement in this protective response. CONCLUSION: Corilagin may alleviate IIRI by modulating ERS-related molecular changes and preserving the intestinal epithelial barrier with NRF2 and ABCG2 contributing to a candidate regulatory module involved in this protective response. These findings provide computational and experimental support for further investigation of Corilagin as a potential intervention for IIRI and illustrate the value of combining multi-source data integration with ensemble machine learning to characterize the multitarget pharmacology of natural products.

articles.title: miR-138-5p: From Multidimensional Tumor-Suppressive Regulatory Networks to Nanocarrier-Based Delivery for Solid Tumor Therapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: MicroRNA-138-5p (miR-138-5p) has been reported to exert tumor-suppressive effects in several solid tumors, and its downregulation has been associated with malignant progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. OBJECTIVE: This review summarizes research trends and current evidence on the molecular functions, regulatory networks, and therapeutic potential of miR-138-5p in solid tumors, with particular emphasis on competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulation and nanocarrier-based delivery strategies. METHODS: Bibliometric analysis and CiteSpace visualization were conducted using English-language original articles and reviews retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection from January 2014 to October 2025. Relevant literature was reviewed to examine miR-138-5p expression, biological functions, target genes, signaling pathways, ceRNA networks, and therapeutic strategies. Studies focused exclusively on hematological malignancies were excluded. RESULTS: Bibliometric mapping identified research clusters spanning multiple solid tumor types, cell-cycle regulation, and proliferation, while metabolic reprogramming and therapeutic resistance emerged as relevant research themes. Mechanistic studies suggest that miR-138-5p regulates proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, autophagy, immune-related signaling, and chemosensitivity through diverse targets and pathways. Long non-coding RNA- and circular RNA-mediated ceRNA networks have been proposed as an additional regulatory layer, although their physiological relevance requires further quantitative validation. Preclinical findings, including exosome-mediated delivery of miR-138-5p, suggest potential for replacement therapy; however, challenges involving delivery efficiency, tumor specificity, biosafety, pharmacokinetics, and manufacturing standardization remain. CONCLUSION: miR-138-5p is a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in solid tumors. Further validation of its context-dependent mechanisms and optimization of targeted delivery strategies are needed to support clinical translation.

articles.title: Palopegteriparatide: Parathyroid Hormone Analog for the Treatment of Chronic Hypoparathyroidism in Adults.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To review the pharmacology, efficacy, and safety of palopegteriparatide for the treatment of chronic hypoparathyroidism in adults. DATA SOURCES: A literature search was conducted in PubMed from September 2015 to August 2026. All relevant publications, package inserts, and clinical trials with palopegteriparatide were reviewed. Keywords used were: palopegteriparatide, hypoparathyroidism, parathyroid hormone (PTH), TransCon PTH, hypocalcemia, PTH(1-34), clinical trials and quality of life. DATA EXTRACTION: All relevant publications, abstracts, package inserts, and clinical trials involving palopegteriparatide were reviewed. DATA SYNTHESIS: Palopegteriparatide is a once-daily subcutaneous injection that uses TransCon technology to treat chronic hypoparathyroidism in adults. Palopegteriparatide led to 93% of participants achieving complete independence from conventional therapy (calcium and active vitamin D) in phase 3 trials. Pill burden decreased from 6.7 at baseline to 0.26 at week 52, and the health-related quality of life of participants significantly increased. The mild-to-moderate adverse effects of palopegteriparatide support its overall favorable tolerability profile.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison to Existing Drugs:Palopegteriparatide is a new PTH analog that mimics physiologic PTH exposure, resulting in more stable serum calcium levels and improved renal handling of calcium and phosphate. CONCLUSION: Palopegteriparatide is the only Food and Drug Administration-approved medication available that addresses PTH deficiency in chronic hypoparathyroidism. It provides a 24-hour continuous release of PTH enabling effective management of PTH insufficiency.

articles.title: Neuropsychiatric adverse event reporting with GLP-1-based therapies: a post-marketing pharmacovigilance analysis using the WHO global individual case safety report database (VigiBase).
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Concerns regarding neuropsychiatric adverse events (NPAEs), including depression and suicidality, have emerged with the expanding use of GLP-1-based therapies across metabolic and weight-management indications. This study aimed to characterize neuropsychiatric adverse-event reporting patterns for GLP-1-based therapies in VigiBase using disproportionality analysis. METHODS: Individual case safety reports entered into the WHO global pharmacovigilance database (VigiBase) from inception through 31 January 2025 were examined. Disproportionality analysis using the information components and the reporting odds ratio was conducted to identify putative safety signals. The full VigiBase reporting background during the study period was used as the comparator. We described the drug-event pairs, mapped signal overlap across agents, evaluated the relationship between reporting frequency and signal magnitude, and conducted stratified analyses by sex and age. RESULTS: Among 899 280 GLP-1RAs-related reports, 19 811 (2.2%) related NPAEs comprised 273 preferred terms and generated 69 positive signals. Semaglutide and liraglutide presented the broadest and most potent signal portfolios, driven chiefly by binge eating (semaglutide, IC₀₂₅ = 3.379; ROR₀₂₅ = 14.483), and aversion (liraglutide, IC₀₂₅ = 3.365; ROR₀₂₅ = 20.512). In contrast, albiglutide was essentially signal negative, and dulaglutide and tirzepatide generated narrower spectra. In addition, semaglutide was positively associated with two "suicide/self-injury" AEs: "depression suicidal" (ROR₀₂₅ = 4.822) and "suicidal ideation" (ROR₀₂₅ = 2.643). CONCLUSIONS: This study identified several potential drug safety signals. However, the estimates were unadjusted and may be influenced by confounding by indication, channelling, notoriety bias, and event competition. Eating-related signals should be interpreted cautiously because they may overlap with the treated population and appetite-related pharmacology of these agents. Given the spontaneous reporting nature of VigiBase, these findings should be interpreted as potential reporting signals rather than evidence of causality. Further well-designed observational studies and prospective clinical investigations are needed to clarify whether GLP-1-based therapies are associated with increased neuropsychiatric risk and to identify patient-level risk modifiers.

articles.title: A Model for Estimating the Risk of Gastrointestinal Bleeding for Patients on Oral Anticoagulants and Interacting Medications.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pharmacodynamic drug-drug interactions (DDI) in patients receiving oral anticoagulants (OAC) may increase the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). The purpose of this study was to develop and validate a GIB model for patients receiving OACs. METHODS: A risk model, Drug Interactions in Oral AntiCoagulants for Risk of Gastrointestinal Bleeding (DIOAC-GIB), was developed to predict GIB based on interacting medications and other patient-specific risk factors for patients on OAC. Inputs for the model were obtained using random-effect meta-analysis or from the literature for the following attributes: exposure to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs); selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors/serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SSRI/SNRIs); aspirin, antiplatelet medications, and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs); age; and GIB history. The model was correlated to existing OAC models (HAS-BLED and DOAC score). RESULTS: GIB risk for OACs was based on pivotal trials (1.16% for apixaban; 3.15% for rivaroxaban; 3.00% for dabigatran; 3.31% for edoxaban; and 2.00% for warfarin). The odds ratio (OR) of GIB for NSAIDs ranged from 1.16 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.84-1.61) for celecoxib to 20.67 (95% CI: 14.56-29.34) for ketorolac. ORs for GIB among SSRI/SNRIs ranged from 1.31 (95% CI: 1.07-1.62) for paroxetine to 1.50 (95% CI: 1.32-1.70) for venlafaxine. Risk of GIB also included persons > 65 years of age (relative risk = 2.50, 95% CI: 1.2-5.5); history of GIB (OR = 5.14, 95% CI: 3.92-6.73); exposure to aspirin (OR = 1.31, 95% CI: 0.93-1.85), antiplatelet medications (OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.73-2.25), and corticosteroids (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.53-1.87); and PPIs reduced GIB risk (OR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.62-0.74). Correlations between the DIOAC-GIB and HAS-BLED and DOAC scores were 0.5 for both (p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: DIOAC-GIB is a novel GIB-risk model that incorporates pharmacodynamic OAC DDIs to assist clinicians and patients to determine a therapeutic plan while accounting for GIB risk. DIOAC-GIB correlates with other bleeding risk scores and may help identify high-risk patients who may benefit from tailored prescribing.

articles.title: Association between perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy and reoperation following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: A TriNetX database study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperlipidemia (HLD) impairs tendon healing and is associated with increased revision risk following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR). While statins may partially mitigate this effect, residual dyslipidemia may impair healing. Ezetimibe, through inhibition of intestinal cholesterol absorption, has demonstrated favorable effects on tendon healing in preclinical studies. OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy is associated with improved postoperative outcomes following ARCR compared with statin monotherapy and patients without HLD. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adult patients undergoing ARCR were stratified into three cohorts based on HLD status and perioperative (± 6 months) lipid-lowering therapy: (1) documented HLD treated with statin-ezetimibe prescriptions, (2) patients without documented HLD or lipid-lowering therapy prescriptions, and (3) documented HLD treated with statin monotherapy prescriptions. Primary comparisons were predefined between cohort 1 and cohorts 2 and 3. Propensity score matching (1:1) adjusted for demographics and comorbidities. Tear size and presence of fatty atrophy and fatty infiltration were not adjusted for. Outcomes occurring within 5 years included revision rotator cuff repair (RCR), conversion to shoulder arthroplasty, and secondary shoulder arthroscopy. RESULTS: After matching, 1,066 patients were included in cohorts 1 and 2 and 1,114 patients in cohorts 1 and 3. Compared with patients without HLD, statin-ezetimibe therapy demonstrated similar rates of revision RCR (5.4% vs. 6.4%; RR 0.853; p = 0.358), conversion to shoulder arthroplasty (RR 1.227; p = 0.470), and secondary arthroscopy (RR 0.846; p = 0.260). Compared with statin monotherapy, statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower rates of revision RCR (5.6% vs. 8.0%; RR 0.697; p = 0.023) and secondary shoulder arthroscopy (7.3% vs. 9.6%; RR 0.757; p = 0.048), while arthroplasty rates remained similar (RR 1.261; p = 0.400). CONCLUSION: Among patients with HLD undergoing ARCR, perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower reoperation rates compared with statin monotherapy and postoperative outcomes comparable to patients without HLD. These findings support further investigation of intensified lipid-lowering therapy, while accounting for tear size and fatty infiltration.

articles.title: Formulation and bioactivity evaluation of titanium dioxide nanoparticles from Coriandrum sativum leaves extract via design of experiments.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to synthesize titanium dioxide nanoparticles using Coriandrum sativum leaf extract as a green reducing and capping agent and to evaluate their antibacterial and antioxidant activities. SIGNIFICANCE: The study highlights an eco-friendly and sustainable approach for nanoparticle synthesis, reducing the use of toxic chemicals and offering potential applications in nanotechnological fields. METHODS: Nanoparticles were synthesized and optimized using a response-surface design. Characterization was performed using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, field emission scanning electron microscopy, and ultraviolet spectroscopy. Antibacterial activity was assessed against Pseudomonas aeruginosa using the well-diffusion method, while antioxidant activity was evaluated through free radical scavenging assays compared with ascorbic acid. RESULTS: The nanoparticles were smooth, spherical, and ranged from 10-40 nm with minimal agglomeration. X-ray diffraction confirmed the anatase crystalline phase. The nanoparticles showed significant antibacterial activity and notable antioxidant potential. The IC50 value determined from the DPPH radical-scavenging assay was 2.96 µg/mL, indicating a strong antioxidant effect of the TiO2 nanoparticles. CONCLUSIONS: Green-synthesized titanium dioxide nanoparticles exhibit effective antibacterial and antioxidant properties, demonstrating promising potential for nanotechnological applications.

articles.title: Area Under the Curve vs Trough-Based Vancomycin Monitoring in Pediatric Patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Trough-based monitoring was previously the primary way to monitor vancomycin; however, 2020 vancomycin consensus guidelines recommend area under the curve (AUC)-based monitoring as the preferred strategy. Data regarding this approach remain limited in the pediatric population. OBJECTIVE: To compare the proportion of pediatric patients achieving therapeutic vancomycin serum concentrations using AUC vs trough-based monitoring and evaluate the safety and efficacy of both strategies. METHODS: This is a single-center retrospective cohort study comparing trough- and Bayesian AUC-based vancomycin monitoring. Patients aged 28 days to 18 years on vancomycin with at least 2 appropriately obtained levels were included. Patients were excluded for suspected or confirmed central nervous system infection, renal dysfunction at vancomycin initiation, neonate or postmenstrual age <44 weeks, or use of continuous vancomycin. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving therapeutic vancomycin serum concentrations. Secondary outcomes included proportion of patients achieving therapeutic goal by the second pharmacokinetic evaluation, time to therapeutic goal, 30- and 90-day all-cause mortality, number of dose adjustments, number of serum concentrations collected, proportion of appropriately timed serum concentrations, and incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI). RESULTS: Eighty-six patients were included: 49 AUC and 37 trough. Overall target attainment was higher in the AUC group (95.9% vs 51.4%; P < .001). The AUC group had a lower final vancomycin dose (P < .001), fewer dose adjustments (P = .004), serum concentrations obtained (P = .02), and more appropriately timed serum concentrations (P = .02). Incidence of AKI and 30- and 90-day all-cause mortality did not differ between groups. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Area under the curve monitoring was associated with higher therapeutic goal attainment, lower final vancomycin doses, higher percentage of appropriately timed serum concentrations, fewer serum concentrations drawn, and fewer dosage adjustments. These findings add pediatric-specific evidence supporting 2020 guideline recommendations and indicate Bayesian area under the curve monitoring is a feasible, resource-efficient strategy in this population.

articles.title: Editorial: Herbal medicine for the treatment of chronic metabolic diseases, volume II.
Identifying Dose-Relevant Covariates With SCOUT: A Case Study of Lorlatinib.
articles.abstract: Molecularly targeted therapeutics, such as lorlatinib, are typically initiated at fixed starting doses with subsequent tolerability-guided modifications, although substantial interindividual variability in pharmacokinetics and drug exposure may influence both efficacy and safety outcomes. Therefore, identifying patient factors associated with individualized dose requirements is an important step toward precision dosing. The aim of this study was to apply the Systematic Covariate Observational Uncovering Technique (SCOUT) framework to explore patient characteristics that may be associated with the individualized optimal dose of lorlatinib. A previously published population pharmacokinetic model was used to estimate individual pharmacokinetic parameters and individualized optimal doses, targeting a trough concentration of 150 ng/mL 3 weeks after treatment initiation. Associations between the estimated optimal dose and patient covariates were examined through exploratory visualization and quantified using multivariate linear regression with Lindeman-Merenda-Gold relative importance analysis. Individualized optimal doses, successfully estimated in all 330 patients, exhibited a wide distribution (mean ± SD: 194 ± 134 mg/day). The exploratory analyses suggested that older age, female sex, and greater renal impairment were associated with lower estimated optimal doses, with sex explaining the largest proportion of the variance. By reframing the covariate analysis around the dose rather than pharmacokinetic parameters, this study provides a clinically interpretable perspective on interindividual variability in dosing requirements. Although exploratory and hypothesis-generating, this study lays a quantitative foundation for future evaluations of precision dosing strategies for lorlatinib.
